articles.title: Prism Shards — R3 DEV
articles.summary: Angular chips of red, blue and olive green scattered over dark metal, glossy with sharp colour jumps. Reads as a rainbow confetti or jelly-bean mosaic; at distance a multicolour mottle averaging to a muddy pastel-bright mix.
articles.what: Small angular prism chips with irregular color transitions. Development study; in-game validation and final review pending. Up close: Soft rounded pebbles or blobs, 30 to 80 px, in saturated red, blue, green, teal, magenta, yellow and orange with blurred edges against a hazy grey-mauve mesh; fine light grain over all. Colours jump between neighbouring cells with no order. From a distance: Reads as a rainbow confetti or jelly-bean mosaic; at distance a multicolour mottle averaging to a muddy pastel-bright mix. Measured spec (average): metal 253, roughness 40, coat 216. Shine: gloss. Metal: full. It brings its own colours.
when: Best on: body, hero panel, sides.
Fits: gt / sports car, show car, open wheel.
how: Click the zone you want to change.
Click the BASE MATERIAL box (it says "Click to choose a base") and type "Prism Shards — R3 DEV" in the SEARCH FINISHES box.
Click it to open the big preview, then click Apply.
Leave BASE COLOR on Use finish's own color to keep its colours.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Hood, roof and sides: cell size reads on wide panels
Not for trim or number panels
Very busy and multi-coloured: use a solid plate or a thick black outline with white fill; plain numbers fail.
None: the mosaic is the pattern
Pairs well with: gloss black, silver, deep red, matte charcoal.
pitfalls: Not sharp angular prism chips: the cells are soft, rounded blobs with blurred edges
Not dark metal: it is bright and colourful, not dark red, blue and olive only
Avoid: thin pinstripes disappear, next to other chunky flake finishes.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 253 (chrome or mirror tier), roughness 40 (high gloss), clearcoat 216 (almost no clearcoat). The spec is almost perfectly flat, one smooth material.
articles.intent_note: Full-finish shelf: the finish carries both its own paint look and its own shine.
articles.paint_advice: It brings its own colours, so leave BASE COLOR on the finish's own colour. Put it next to a plain zone of the opposite sheen (matte beside gloss, warm beside cool) so the colours have a calm neighbour. Avoid: thin pinstripes disappear, next to other chunky flake finishes.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: none: the mosaic is the pattern; a clean number plate or solid stripe
Patterns to avoid: camo, weave or flake patterns: clash with the cells; fine line patterns: moire
Spec overlays that work: no sparkle spec: sparkle is already low, but the colours carry the look; gloss-only spec to sharpen the metal
Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.
